policies.name: Devices running EOL OS-Mock Mobile
policies.description: This policy identifies operating systems deemed EOL (End of Life) by the manufacturer. The EOL for software means that the software has reached the end of its predefined support period and will be retired. Beyond this date, the software will no longer receive feature enhancements, maintenance, or security updates

policies.name: Established Connection Using Weak TLS Cipher Suite
policies.description: This policy detects active sessions communicating over weak, deprecated cipher suites. Services allowing these established connections should be audited and transitioned to secure, recommended alternatives to enforce modern cryptographic standards.

policies.name: Attempted Connection Using Weak TLS Cipher Suite
policies.description: This policy detects connection requests attempting to negotiate weak cipher suites that rely on deprecated cryptographic algorithms. While these suites still provide basic encryption, they lack modern security standards and their usage should be monitored for phase-out.

policies.name: Suspicious TLS communication
policies.description:
This policy monitors network traffic to detect and alert on instances of protocol tunneling hidden within unexpected or anomalous Transport Layer Security (TLS) connections.
It specifically identifies situations where unauthorized protocols or restricted data streams are being encapsulated and smuggled inside seemingly legitimate, encrypted TLS sessions to bypass standard firewall controls or security boundaries.

policies.name: Established Connection Using Insecure TLS Cipher Suite
policies.description: This policy detects active, successfully established connections utilizing insecure cipher suites. Because these sessions are exposed to interception and compromise, they should be terminated and the underlying service misconfigurations resolved.

policies.name: Attempted Connection Using Insecure TLS Cipher Suite
policies.description: This policy detects handshake requests attempting to negotiate insecure cipher suites that provide no meaningful cryptographic protection. These attempts expose communications to interception and should be blocked.
